name: Aighon
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: only wordlists and sociolinguistic surveys of the region (Chowning 1969; Johnston 1980; MacKenzie et al. 2013 on neighboring Bebeli); nothing describing Aighon stress

sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm. 2002. Kaulong. In Lynch, Ross & Crowley (eds), The Oceanic Languages, 387-409. Richmond: Curzon. [SISTER LANGUAGE Kaulong, kaul1240, same Pasismanua chain - context only]
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: held in print at Harvard (Tozzer Library, call number OC. L 991 o; Widener Library, call number PL6172.L963 2002x); the library holds the journal volume but the item itself was not found; ask your own library for a scan or interlibrary loan
sources.harvard_location: Tozzer Library, call number OC. L 991 o; Widener Library, call number PL6172 .L963 2002x
sources.note: p. 388 sec. 1.3: 'Kaulong stress generally falls on the final syllable of a verb and on the penultimate syllable of a noun.' Not about Aighon; nearest described relative, noted for context only.

sources.citation: OLAC: resources in and about the Aighon language [aix] (state of Nov 2025, via the Internet Archive).
sources.note: Lists only Glottolog, Ethnologue, LINGUIST List and the two Kaipuleohone audio items; no language description.

sources.citation: Spencer (Bullock), Juliann, Sara Van Cott & Bonnie MacKenzie. 2013. A Sociolinguistic Survey of Bebeli. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2013-003. Dallas: SIL International. 96 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Contains an Aighon wordlist (Zebu village, 2009, transcriber Seonok Jung; Appendix C Table 14, Appendix D.5 pp. 76ff, 170 items) in IPA with no stress marks anywhere in the document; Aighon otherwise mentioned only for lexicostatistics and cultural ties.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2007. Change Request 2007-001 (submitted by Iljae Jung, SIL-PNG): change reference name of [aix] from Aigon to Aighon. 8 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; only segmental notes (g vs gh contrast: gon 'different' vs ghon 'above'; intervocalic voiced stops prenasalised; autoglottonym Eighon).

sources.citation: Chowning, Ann. 1996. Relations among languages of West New Britain: an assessment of recent theories and evidence. In M. Ross (ed.), Studies in languages of New Britain and New Ireland 1, 7-62. Pacific Linguistics C-135.
sources.note: Sec. 8.3.1.1 'Psohoh' (pp. 34-37) summarises the Bao (northern Psohoh = Aighon area) dialect from Johnston's 1981 typescript: grammar, a 67-item wordlist, and one phonology paragraph (voiced/voiceless stop contrast, flap, fricatives, /w/); no statement about stress.
sources.venue: Studies in languages of New Britain and New Ireland 1

sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm. 1988. Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian languages of western Melanesia. Pacific Linguistics C-98. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201.R67 1988)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201 .R67 1988
sources.note: Psohoh (= Bao, 'Psohoh (Aigon)', informant Justice Kalambrek of Zebu; source Johnston 1981) appears only in ch. 5 sound-correspondence tables and subgrouping discussion; no stress statement for Psohoh/Aighon.

sources.citation: Chowning, Ann. 1985. Rapid lexical change and aberrant Melanesian languages: Sengseng and its neighbours. In Pawley & Carrington (eds), Austronesian linguistics at the 15th Pacific Science Congress, 169-198. Pacific Linguistics C-88.
sources.note: Psohoh mentioned pp. 170, 174 (Johnston 1980b:124,127 tentatively posits seven vowels for Psohoh), 176 and notes 13-14 (consonant correspondences); nothing on stress in any Pasismanua language.
sources.venue: Austronesian linguistics at the 15th Pacific Science Congress

sources.citation: Duhe, Nathan Lee. 2024. Phonology Essentials Aighon [aix]. Unpublished ms., 29 pp. (draft, July 2024). SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 100036; sec. 5 'Pitch/Stress' p. 24.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only known phonological description of Aighon; its TOC shows a dedicated Pitch/Stress section (p. 24). Would settle the question first-hand. Request from SIL PNG (Ukarumpa) Language Resources / archive_png@sil.org or the author.

sources.citation: Johnston, Raymond L. 1981. An introduction to the Bao language of the New Britain Whiteman family. Typescript, SIL, Ukarumpa. (Bao = northern Psohoh dialect, i.e. the Aighon area; cited by Chowning 1996 and Ross 1988.)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Earliest sketch of the Bao/Psohoh (Aighon) variety with a phoneme inventory; an SIL-style introduction of this period usually includes a suprasegmentals note. Possibly held in the SIL PNG library at Ukarumpa or in Chowning's/Ross's papers.

sources.citation: SIL-PNG Aighon programme materials by Iljae & Seonok Jung (c. 2007-2009): any Organised Phonology Data / orthography paper for Aighon [aix] (existence not confirmed; the Jungs submitted ISO CR 2007-001 and transcribed the 2009 Zebu wordlist).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: An OPD sheet, if one was filed at Ukarumpa, would carry a 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)' entry; not in the public SIL archive catalogue, so ask SIL PNG directly together with the Duhe ms.

sources.citation: Johnston, Raymond L. 1980. The languages and communities of the Kimbe Bay region. In R. L. Johnston (ed.), Language, communication and development in New Britain, 107-158. Ukarumpa: SIL. (SIL archives 39242)

sources.note: pp. 124-127 contain Johnston's tentative phonemicisation of Psohoh (Bao) per Chowning 1985:174; may include a remark on stress. Print only (SIL PNG; held in Australian/PNG libraries).
sources.venue: Language, communication and development in New Britain

sources.note: An SIL-PNG Orthography and Phonology Description is a short standardized phonology data sheet (phoneme chart, syllable patterns, phonological and orthographic conventions, sample text); such sheets usually carry a one-line stress/tone convention note; contents unseen. Possibly the precursor of the known Duhe 2024 Phonology Essentials (sec. 5 'Pitch/Stress'), but a distinct document (different genre, year and co-author) — verification to decide whether to merge with a work listed here (placeholder 'any OPD for Aighon', attributed there to the Jungs, existence unconfirmed).
